title: Proof of the mad conjecture and its coloring applications
summary: For a finite graph $G$, the maximum average degree $\operatorname{mad}(G)$ is the largest average degree of a nonempty subgraph of $G$. Hendrey, Norin and Wood asked whether this parameter is partitionable, that is, whether for all positive reals $a,b$ every graph $G$ with $\operatorname{mad}(G)<a+b$ admits a vertex partition $V(G)=A\cup B$ with $\operatorname{mad}(G[A])<a$ and $\operatorname{mad}(G[B])<b$.
